sampling_model.design: Four independent destructive population snapshots at times \(0,h,2h,3h\).
sampling_model.units: At time \(kh\), \(n_k\) independent units are sampled from the marginal law of \(Y_k\); no unit is followed across time.
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is present; the structural target is the continuous-time interaction generator \(G\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Sample means and covariances form \(\widehat z\). On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) and \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\). On a regular noncyclic finite branch, the local residual projection gives \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) and \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{loc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\); globally certified initialization and labeling remain the explicit open question.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2.1 characterizes and generically selects a transition from two covariance congruences and mean equations when the propagated noise covariance is known.
Corollary 2.1 states that three time points identify the transition and constant load under its known-noise conditions.
Theorems 6 and 8 recover deterministic affine dynamics from two supplied covariance pairs and mean pairs under generic spectral and probe conditions.
Theorem 1 states that QWENDY returns the ground-truth linearized transition from four supplied covariance matrices under invertibility and simple-spectrum conditions.
Algorithms 1 and 2 alternate Schrödinger-bridge trajectory reconstruction with transition and process-noise updates for direct state snapshots.
Theorems 2 and 4 certify Newton convergence and equality or distinctness of supplied approximate roots of square polynomial systems.
The paper derives concentration and normal approximation for empirical spectral-projector error under Gaussian sampling.
Theorem 2.6 makes likelihood-ratio limits at semialgebraic boundaries and singularities depend on tangent cones.

body.tldr: Four independent Gaussian snapshots can identify a stable continuous-time linear mechanism even when every observed covariance contains the same unknown positive-definite measurement component, but the answer is a stratified fiber rather than automatically one matrix. With three snapshots, raw compatibility holds exactly when \(\lVert H_0^{-1/2}d_0\rVert_2=\lVert H_1^{-1/2}d_1\rVert_2\); the compatible transitions form an \(O(p-1)\) torsor when \(d_0\ne0\) and an \(O(p)\) torsor when \(d_0=0\), giving continuous ambiguity generically for \(p\ge3\) and already at \(p=2\) on the zero-displacement elbow. A fourth snapshot identifies generically through the rational map \(K_1K_0^{-1}\), while stability, the principal-logarithm cut, Stein reconstruction, and strict noise positivity decide structural compatibility. The same stabilizer dimension equals information nullity; on finite strata the exact worst-case number of compatible explanations is \(2^{p-1}\), and this bound is attained. Regular branches admit perturbation bounds and Gaussian moment inference. Supplying \(E\) yields this paper's stable, embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise subclass of the broader Aalto--Lamoline--Goncalves model, not equality with that model class. Certified initialization and stable labeling of every noncyclic finite branch remain open.

project_justification.gap: Published snapshot-identification results either use supplied state covariances or work in broader known-noise transition models without classifying the fiber created by one unknown common additive covariance. In particular, a supplied \(E\) places the present stable, embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise system inside the broader Aalto--Lamoline--Goncalves class, which also permits known process covariance, arbitrary invertible discrete-time dynamics, and finite-second-moment non-Gaussian laws; it does not make the two model classes equal.
project_justification.niche: Common measurement noise cancels from adjacent covariance differences but re-enters through level-covariance positivity. With three snapshots this gives an exactly computable one-vector orthogonal matching problem, including a zero-displacement \(O(p)\) elbow, while the fourth snapshot adds a second congruence that generically collapses the stabilizer through a rational Krylov identity.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the exact three-snapshot norm certificate and \(O(p-r)\) classification, an if-and-only-if four-snapshot block Gram certificate, a bijective admissibility map, the complete exceptional-stratum classification, and the sharp attainable finite-fiber maximum \(2^{p-1}\), together with rational perturbation theory and branchwise inference. It also identifies the precise supplied-noise subclass relation and retains certified global initialization and branch labeling as the remaining open construction problem.

body.related_work: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 provides the closest congruence architecture. Its published class allows known process covariance \(Q\), arbitrary invertible discrete-time dynamics, and finite-second-moment non-Gaussian laws. After a supplied measurement covariance \(E\) is subtracted, the model studied here is only its stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, \(Q=0\) subclass; the inherited consequence used here is the consecutive latent-covariance congruence, not equality of model classes or an exact reduction to every part of their theorem. It does not provide the present two-probe residual-rank classification or the sharp \(2^{p-1}\) admissible finite-fiber maximum. WangEtAl2024 proves a three-time-point result for deterministic affine dynamics from supplied state moments and motivates the \(\texttt{covar\_lin\_dyn}\) consumer. QWENDY2025 uses four supplied covariance matrices and simple spectra to resolve a homogeneous congruence problem, but it contains neither an unknown common additive covariance nor the exact three-snapshot norm and stabilizer classification proved here. MorimotoKashima2025 and InoueEtAl2026 estimate stochastic linear dynamics from direct snapshot marginals by Schrödinger-bridge optimization without a global common-noise identification certificate. Blevins2017 analyzes continuous-time aliases and motivates the principal-logarithm strip after the transition is recovered. KoltchinskiiLounici2017 supplies spectral perturbation tools, while HauensteinSottile2012 supplies root certificates; neither solves basis-invariant finite-branch enumeration with matrix-inequality filters. ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 and Drton2009 locate set inference and singular asymptotics around the regular-stratum results. KongEtAl2023 studies process and measurement covariance identification from a paired stationary time series with known system matrices, a different information regime from destructive marginal snapshots.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact population conditions--spectral matching, block Gram equality, and the three-snapshot whitened norm equality--must not be imposed as empirical accept-or-reject equalities, because unconstrained noisy sample moments satisfy them with probability zero. On a finite population stratum, the block certificate yields \(2^q\) raw sign completions; when \(q\ge1\), the determinant test removes at least half before the principal-logarithm calculation, and the sharp worst-case admissible output size is \(2^{p-1}\). On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) is the off-model rational estimator used by the perturbation theorem. The radius \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\) guarantees that its full plug-in reconstruction is defined, whereas the smaller radius \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\) also preserves the stability, logarithm, Stein, and reconstructed-covariance positivity filters; neither radius forces noisy moments onto the exact population fiber. On a noncyclic finite stratum, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is a population-branch-centered residual estimator, not a globally implementable branch finder until certified initialization and labeling are solved. The two structural plug-ins are \(\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\) and \(\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\), each with initial-mean coordinate \(\widehat m_0\).
body.honest_scope: The exact population three-snapshot norm certificate, its \(O(p-r)\) fibers, the generic four-snapshot frontier, stabilizer dimension, the sharp attainable finite-stratum maximum of \(2^{p-1}\) compatible explanations, the information-nullity identity, cyclic perturbation bounds, and the local regular-branch limit law are theorem-level deliverables. The \(d_0=0\) elbow has continuous \(O(p)\) ambiguity already at \(p=2\); when \(p=2\) and \(d_0\ne0\), the raw fiber is only zero-dimensional and admissibility filters may leave one or more isolated candidates. Any unknown-common-noise supermodel containing the deterministic Gaussian subclass inherits its three-snapshot nonidentification witnesses. Supplying \(E\) gives only the stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise subclass of AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022; the broader published class also permits known \(Q\), arbitrary invertible discrete-time transitions, and non-Gaussian finite-second-moment laws. The global certified initializer, complete branch certificate, stable empirical labeling, and simultaneous coverage across all noncyclic finite branches remain open. No uniform inference is claimed at branch collisions, positivity boundaries, logarithm cuts, or stabilizer-dimension jumps, and exact population equalities are not empirical testing rules.
